clue.text: Tin oil-vessel, lousy sort, crossing others so?

parts.note: a tin is a can
a tanker is a ship that carries oil

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange, so the letters of lousy are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A slovenly fellow on an oil tanker keeps upsetting his shipmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' looks like a noun after 'lousy', but it is the anagram signal. The question mark flags that the definition describes how someone behaves when crossing others.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who crosses or contradicts others habitually acts in a bad-tempered, quarrelsome manner.

parts.note: flights are the feathered tails of arrows, and by extension arrows themselves

explanation.surface: Restrictions on flights heading north.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrow something is to restrict or confine it, the verb sense of limit.

parts.note: a way of doing things is a method or system

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: flights follow a system used overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link this clue to the previous one, making the two read as one sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abroad is out of the country, gone from home.

clue.text: Coal burns, you could say, as cabbage

indicators.note: a phrase that tells the solver the letters come from how the words are spoken

parts.note: coal plus Burns, whose first name is Rabbie: Robert Burns, Scotland's national poet

explanation.surface: A remark that a vegetable burns like coal.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns is not a verb here: it is Robert 'Rabbie' Burns, the Scottish poet, so 'Coal Rabbie' is said and the vegetable is written.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohlrabi is a turnip-shaped variety of the cabbage family, Brassica oleracea.

clue.text: Raced in Rugby and Slough, say

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union
to slough is to shed, as a snake sheds its skin

explanation.surface: Someone sped through the English towns of Rugby and Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby and Slough look like a pair of English towns; Rugby gives RU (Rugby Union) and Slough is the verb meaning cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushed and raced both mean moved or went at great speed.

clue.text: Education of young person at university-earning?

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university, a British usage
earning money is bringing it in, so bringing stands for earning

explanation.surface: Asks whether a young person should be studying at university or out earning.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's upbringing is the rearing and training given while growing up.

parts.note: read as a lamp whose flame is carried inside a glass case, rather than a torch taken along as a precaution

explanation.surface: A torch taken along as a precaution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just in case' suggests precaution, but the case is the glass housing that holds the flame.
explanation.definitionFit: This portable lamp encloses its flame in a protective case of glass or horn.

clue.text: Mechanical vendor gives St. Michael no change

indicators.note: change signals that the letters of St Michael and no are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A machine refuses to give St Michael any coins back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no change' reads as a vending machine keeping the money, but 'change' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This coin-operated machine dispenses goods automatically, a vendor run by mechanism.

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, a fresh sorting of the letters of Abersoch

explanation.surface: Someone launches a holiday resort in Abersoch, a seaside village in north Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Abersoch really is a seaside resort, which hides that 'resort' means re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject is to raise it or open it up for discussion.

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit or restrict
L is the letter on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Banning a learner driver from the road would make them a pedestrian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' reads as someone walking, but it is the adjective meaning dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means dull and uninspired, as does banal.

parts.note: read as a document issued for every birth a midwife delivers, rather than a permit for a courier's parcels

explanation.surface: A permit is needed for every parcel a courier drops off.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'delivery' is a birth, and each one is followed by an official birth document.
explanation.definitionFit: A certificate is an official document, like a licence, attesting to a fact such as a birth.

clue.text: Some unseen owls enough for a poet?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A poet wonders whether a few invisible owls would be sufficient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a poet' marks an archaic word found in old verse.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the old poetic form of sufficient, used by writers like Shakespeare.

clue.text: Bad temper in N.E. is unsurpassed

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of temper, in and NE are spoiled into a different order

parts.note: NE is north-east, written as letters

explanation.surface: Short tempers in the north-east of England are beyond compare.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pre-eminent stands above all rivals, unbeaten and unequalled.

definitions.meaning: the heavens are the air and sky surrounding the earth
a mood or tone, as in a room full of tension

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at an emotional moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the envelope of gases round the planet and the pervading mood of a place.

clue.text: Means to experiment with cricket underground

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
the Tube is London's Underground railway

explanation.surface: Trying out cricket on the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass laboratory vessel used for carrying out chemical trials.

indicators.note: clutching means holding inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an aga was an Ottoman military commander
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: An Ottoman officer grips his last journal.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of things to be done or discussed, much like a schedule in a diary.

definitions.meaning: military practice on the parade ground
making holes, as with a power tool

explanation.surface: A complaint that exercise is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like tedious, but it means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both disciplined practice and making holes with a bit.

clue.text: Large bottle, enough for standard cricket-side?

parts.note: a standard is a flag or banner
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A big bottle that might satisfy a whole cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field divides into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large vessel for wine or cider, usually with a handle.

definitions.meaning: the full first name of Nye Bevan, the Welsh politician who founded the NHS
an older name for vitamin B1

explanation.surface: Asks whether the founder of the NHS had a vitamin.
explanation.walkthrough: Nye was short for the Welsh name of Bevan, the minister who launched Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a Welsh given name and an older term for vitamin B1.

clue.text: Flourish a bowl of dietary fibre

parts.note: bran is cereal husk eaten as dietary fibre
a dish is a bowl

explanation.surface: Someone waves about a bowl of breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flourish' could be a noun or mean thrive, but it is the verb meaning wave about.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish a sword or stick is to wave it about showily.

clue.text: Where nurses work, approaching the middle

definitions.meaning: read as two words, the hospital rooms nurses work in

explanation.surface: Nurses work at the heart of the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it locates hospital staff; as one it means moving towards the centre.

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the phrase is cut off

parts.note: in full means entirely

explanation.surface: Is it wicked to give over most of a Sunday?
explanation.definitionFit: Sinful and wicked both describe immoral conduct.

clue.text: Mistakenly, I place Rhyl as the source of this cheese.

indicators.note: mistakenly shows the letters of I, place and Rhyl are set out wrongly

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly says Rhyl, a seaside town in north Wales, is where a cheese comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: The town in south Wales gives its name to a crumbly white cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh town that gave its name to the white cheese first made there.

clue.text: … man there displays novel ring, back to front

indicators.note: back to front tells the solver to read the joined pieces in reverse

parts.note: novel means new
a ring is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: a Welshman shows off a newly made ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the previous clue, so 'there' is Wales; NEWO is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Welsh given name, so a man from the land the previous clue names.

parts.note: kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A southern family goes into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' reads as a verb but is the noun meaning an animal's pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is an animal's pelt.

indicators.note: perhaps suggests that the letters of trees could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Trees that may have been pruned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipped' suggests pruned trees, but it means curt in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipped speech is brief and curt.

definitions.meaning: brief wavering movements, as of a candle
North American woodpeckers of the genus Colaptes

explanation.surface: Birds in America quiver and flap.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both wavering movements of light and a group of New World woodpeckers.

parts.note: brainy means clever

indicators.note: planned suggests the letters of as and I are arranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A clever person boasts of being brainy by design.
explanation.definitionFit: The intellectual elite of a society, its cultured and learned people.
